s: Under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement signed by Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan in August 2026, what does an armed attack on one party signify?
o: An attack on all GCC members
An attack only on the party directly targeted
An attack on all three parties
An attack on all members of the Islamic Military Counter Terrorism Coalition
x: The agreement provides that an armed attack on one of Saudi Arabia, Türkiye or Pakistan is treated as an attack on all three. It does not extend this automatic commitment to all GCC members or to the Islamic Military Counter Terrorism Coalition.

s: Which of the following about the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement is NOT correct?
o: Its Permanent Secretariat is in Türkiye
It was signed in August 2026 by Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan
It builds on the 2025 Saudi–Pakistan Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement
It had been under work for about three years
x: The Permanent Secretariat is in Saudi Arabia, not Türkiye.

s: In which year was the Bandung Conference held?
x: The Bandung (Asian-African) Conference was held in 1955.

s: Which of the following is true of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement?
o: It includes a confirmed Pakistani nuclear guarantee.
It makes the three parties members of NATO.
Its full text and operational obligations are not public.
x: The pact is not NATO, its text and duties are not public, and there is no confirmed Pakistani nuclear guarantee.

s: Which defence arrangement–year pair is correctly matched?
x: Baghdad Pact/CENTO is 1955; Arab League Joint Defence Treaty 1950, Peninsula Shield Force 1984 and IMCTC 2015.

s: The Saudi-led 14-nation Maritime Defence Alliance focuses on which area?
o: Persian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz and Gulf of Oman
Red Sea, Bab el-Mandeb and Gulf of Aden
Red Sea, Suez Canal and Mediterranean
Arabian Sea, Gulf of Oman and Strait of Hormuz
x: The alliance operates in the Red Sea, Bab el-Mandeb and Gulf of Aden.

s: Which is the majority Muslim sect in Iran?
x: Iran is the Islamic country where Shia Islam is the majority sect; most other Muslim-majority countries are Sunni.

s: Who was re-elected President of Zambia in 2026 with 61.4% of about 5 million votes?
x: Hakainde Hichilema won a second term with 61.4% of the vote.

s: Former Ecuadorian President Lenín Moreno was sentenced to 5 years in the Sinohydro bribery case over which project?
x: The Sinohydro case concerned bribes over the Coca Codo Sinclair hydro project.

s: Who was elected Chairman of ECOWAS in July 2026?
x: Senegal's President Bassirou Diomaye Faye was elected ECOWAS Chairman.

s: What was the new name given in June 2026 to the US Indo-Pacific Command?
x: The US Indo-Pacific Command was renamed back to US Pacific Command, abbreviated USPACOM, in June 2026. It had been renamed Indo-Pacific Command in 2018; the other command names do not represent this change.

s: In 2026, which country sought compensation from South Africa for xenophobic violence?
x: Ghana is seeking compensation from South Africa, not the reverse.

s: Which became the first Arab country to bar persons under 15 from creating social media accounts or posting and liking content?
x: The UAE was the first Arab country to impose this under-15 restriction, giving platforms 12 months to comply.

s: Which original BRICS member did not join the World AI Cooperation Organization (WAICO)?
x: India was the only original BRICS member not to join the Shanghai-based, 29-country WAICO.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the August 2026 renaming of Lake Ontario?
o: The new name applies only to US federal use.
Canada also adopted the name Lake America.
The Gulf of Mexico had earlier been renamed the Gulf of America.
Lake Michigan is the only Great Lake wholly within the US.
x: Canada kept the name Lake Ontario; the order applies only to US federal use.

s: Abelardo de la Espriella was sworn in on 7 August 2026 as the 36th President of which country?
x: He became Colombia's 36th President (2026–2030), succeeding Gustavo Petro.

s: Who among the following were the first women to walk to both the North and South Poles?
x: Ann Daniels and Caroline Hamilton became the first women to walk to both poles (2002).

s: Where is the headquarters of ECOWAS?
x: ECOWAS, set up in 1975, has its headquarters at Abuja, Nigeria.

s: In which country did the design of the LHB coaches that India supplies to Bangladesh Railway originate?
x: The LHB design is German. Exports resumed after about 10 years, not five.

s: Who was elected the 23rd President of Bangladesh on 20 August 2026?
x: BNP's Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir won with 255 votes in the first contested presidential election in 35 years; Tarique Rahman is PM.

s: Which of the following about Nepal's ban on Indian mango imports is NOT correct?
o: Affected varieties included Alphonso, Dasheri, Kesar and Banganapalli
Nepal became the second country after Japan to impose such a ban
Nepal became the second country after China to impose such a ban
The ban was imposed over pesticide residues
x: Nepal was the second country after Japan, not China, to ban Indian mangoes over pesticide residues.

s: Which payment linkage was launched during Nepal Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal's India visit (5–7 June 2026)?
x: UPI–NPI peer-to-peer payments were launched during the visit, along with a Bhashini MoU and handover of 84 reconstruction projects.

s: Min Aung Hlaing was sworn in as President of which country on 10 April 2026?
x: Min Aung Hlaing was sworn in as President of Myanmar on 10 April 2026. General Ye Win Oo became the new army chief.

s: Who made Myanmar's first official presidential visit to India during 30 May–3 June 2026?
x: Myanmar President U Min Aung Hlaing made the visit.

s: Mekong-Ganga ICCR scholarships for Myanmar were increased from 36 to how many from 2026?
x: The scholarships were raised from 36 to 100 from 2026.

s: Which Nepal Prime Minister said the Kalapani–Lipulekh–Limpiyadhura dispute should be resolved objectively through diplomacy?
x: Nepal PM Balendra Shah ('Balen') made this statement.

s: Nepal plans to export how much hydropower to India in a decade?
x: Nepal plans to export 10,000 MW to India in a decade, not five years.

s: Which connectivity initiatives were highlighted in the India–Myanmar engagement outcomes?
o: Kaladan Multi-Modal project and India–Myanmar–Thailand Trilateral Highway
x: The outcomes highlighted the Kaladan project via Sittwe Port and the India–Myanmar–Thailand Trilateral Highway.

s:
Assertion (A): Myanmar is India’s only ASEAN neighbour with both a land and a maritime boundary.
Reason (R): The Mekong–Ganga Cooperation includes China and Bangladesh.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Assertion A is true: Myanmar is India’s only ASEAN neighbour with both land and maritime boundaries. Reason R is false because the Mekong–Ganga Cooperation comprises India, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam, not China and Bangladesh.

s: Up to what distance did India's Free Movement Regime with Myanmar, now suspended, allow visa-free movement?
x: The FMR allowed 16 km of visa-free movement and was suspended by India, not Myanmar.

s: What is the length of the India–Myanmar border?
x: The 1,643 km border runs through Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur and Mizoram.

s: According to India’s position in the Kalapani–Lipulekh–Limpiyadhura dispute, where is the source of the Kali/Mahakali River located?
x: India maintains that the source of the Kali/Mahakali River is near Kalapani, in the Pithoragarh area of Uttarakhand. Limpiyadhura is the location identified by Nepal in its claim, making it the most tempting alternative.

s: Lipulekh Pass is used for the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra and for trade between India and which country?
x: Lipulekh is an India–China trade route and a Kailash Mansarovar Yatra route, not an India–Nepal trade route.

s: What is the capacity of the delayed India–Nepal Pancheshwar project?
x: Pancheshwar is 5,040 MW; 10,000 MW is Nepal's planned hydropower export to India in a decade.

s: At what age did Balendra (Balen) Shah, sworn in as Nepal's PM in March 2026, become its youngest PM?
x: He was sworn in on 27 March 2026 aged 35, Nepal's youngest PM.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the political change in Nepal in 2026?
o: The change followed the Gen Z protests of September 2025
Balendra Shah became the first Prime Minister of Madhesh descent
The Rastriya Swatantra Party formed a coalition after failing to win a majority
Sushila Karki served as interim Prime Minister before the new government
x: The RSP won about two-thirds of the seats on 5 March 2026, a clear majority, so no coalition was needed.

s: With which country is the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Project, including Sittwe port, associated?
x: The Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Project is located in Myanmar and includes the Sittwe port component.

s: The India–Myanmar–Thailand Trilateral Highway is about how long?
x: The Trilateral Highway is 1,360 km; 1,643 km is the India–Myanmar border.

s: India's LHB coach supply to Bangladesh is part of a 2024 contract for how many coaches?
x: The 2024 contract covers 200 coaches in 7 variants; the first rake had 19 coaches.

s: The Mechi Bridge connects which of the following places?
x: The Mechi Bridge connects Panitanki in India with Kakarvitta in Nepal. Sabroom–Ramgarh refers to Maitri Setu, while the other pairings do not represent the Mechi Bridge connection.

s: For which country was Operation Brahma (2025), India's relief operation, carried out?
x: Operation Brahma (2025) and Operation Sadbhav (2024) were relief operations for Myanmar; Operation Amistad aided Venezuela.

s: Which of the following is NOT a member of the Mekong–Ganga Cooperation?
x: Mekong–Ganga = India, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam; China and Bangladesh are not members.

s:
Consider the following statements about Nepal's PM Balendra (Balen) Shah:
1. He belongs to the Rastriya Swatantra Party.
2. He was the interim PM before the March 2026 election.
3. He is Nepal's first PM of Madhesh descent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Sushila Karki was the interim PM; Balen Shah is the elected PM.

s: Which of the following states does NOT share a border with Myanmar?
x: The 1,643 km India–Myanmar border touches Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur and Mizoram, not Tripura.

s: Operation Sunrise (2019) is associated with India and which neighbouring country?
x: Operation Sunrise (2019), like Hot Pursuit (2015), is listed among India–Myanmar operations.

s: Which treaty, signed after the Anglo-Nepalese War, made the Kali (Mahakali) river Nepal's western boundary?
x: The Treaty of Sugauli (1816) fixed the Kali/Mahakali as Nepal's western boundary, the root of the Kalapani dispute.

s: Which country became the latest, in June 2026, to accept India's UPI?
x: UPI is accepted in 9 countries; Cambodia was the latest, in June 2026.

s: Maitri Setu over the Feni river connects Sabroom in India with which place in Bangladesh?
x: Maitri Setu over the Feni links Sabroom (Tripura) with Ramgarh (Bangladesh); Kakarvitta is in Nepal.

s: Surya Kiran is a joint military exercise between India and which country?
x: Surya Kiran is the India-Nepal army exercise.

s: The Jhulaghat bridge over the Kali river connects India with which country?
x: Jhulaghat bridge over the Kali links India and Nepal.

s: Who is the Prime Minister of Bangladesh?
x: Tarique Rahman of the BNP is PM; Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was elected the 23rd President in August 2026.

s: The ASI–National Museum of Denmark MoU concerns the wreck of which Danish ship that sank near Karaikal in 1619?
x: The MoU concerns the wreck of the Danish ship Øresund, which sank in 1619 near Karaikal, Puducherry.

s: Which cultural diplomacy initiative–location pair is correctly matched?
o: Swami Vivekananda statue – Indian Consulate, Chicago
x: The Vivekananda statue was unveiled at the Indian Consulate, Chicago; the Vande Mataram event was in Dubai, the Shivaji statue in Israel and the Sushruta statue at RCS Edinburgh.

s: What was the principal purpose of Operation Amistad undertaken by India?
o: Securing subsea cables through underwater drones
x: Operation Amistad provided aid to earthquake-hit Venezuela, including more than 35 tonnes of aid through an IAF C-17, an Army field hospital and two BHISHM Cubes. The Maldives vaccine assistance, UNRWA support and subsea-cable initiative were separate developments.

s: India's CAG signed an audit cooperation MoU with the Supreme Audit Institution of which country?
x: The MoU was between India's CAG and Israel's Supreme Audit Institution.

s: With whom did PM Modi discuss the long-term India–Venezuela energy partnership in New Delhi?
x: PM Modi held the talks with Venezuela's Acting President Delcy Rodríguez.

s: What is the capital of Tanzania?
x: Tanzania's capital is Dodoma, not Dar es Salaam.

s: With which scheme is the India Ship Technology Centre associated?
x: The India Ship Technology Centre is linked with the Shipbuilding Development Scheme, which is distinct from the Financial Assistance Scheme.

s: Which Korean body, representing 300+ marine-equipment firms, set up a presence in Mumbai under the India–South Korea shipbuilding partnership?
x: KOMEA (Korea Marine Equipment Association) represents more than 300 firms and opened a presence in Mumbai.

s: Where is the 200-acre IIT Madras Zanzibar campus located?
x: The campus is spread over 200 acres in the Fumba Peninsula; it is the first international IIT campus.

s: The ACME–Mitsubishi Gas Chemical agreement involving 1,00,000 tonnes per year of green methanol was significant because it was described as what?
o: India’s first international nuclear fuel deal
India’s first international green marine fuel deal
India’s first bilateral water technology deal
x: The agreement was described as India’s first international green marine fuel deal and involved 1,00,000 tonnes per year of green methanol. Nuclear fuel, water technology and submarine cable agreements refer to different developments.

s: Which of the following statements about the I-2SEA submarine cable announced in July 2026 is NOT correct?
o: It lands at Machilipatnam and Mumbai.
It connects Singapore, Malaysia and India.
x: The incorrect statement is that the cable lands at Machilipatnam and Mumbai. The stated landing points are Machilipatnam and South Chennai; Mumbai is the headquarters of Tata Communications, one of the associated partners.

s: In which year did India and Tanzania become strategic partners?
x: India and Tanzania set up a strategic partnership in 2023; IIT Madras Zanzibar is India's first overseas IIT.

s: Which shipyard–location pair is correctly matched?
x: Hindustan Shipyard is at Visakhapatnam; Mazagon Dock is in Mumbai, GRSE in Kolkata and Alang in Gujarat.

s: Where is the first international campus of an IIT located?
x: IIT Madras Zanzibar in Tanzania is the first international IIT campus.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Alang in Gujarat is India's major ship-recycling centre.
2. India's Recycling of Ships Act was passed in 2019.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Alang (Gujarat) is the ship-recycling hub and the Recycling of Ships Act was passed in 2019, in line with the Hong Kong Convention.

s: Which of the following about India's shipbuilding initiatives is NOT correct?
o: Sagarmala Finance Corporation Ltd is India's first maritime NBFC
The Maritime Development Fund has ₹25,000 crore
India aims to be among the top five shipbuilders by 2030
The proposed mega shipyard is at Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu
x: The target is top 10 by 2030 and top 5 by 2047.

s: PM Modi became the second Indian PM to receive Indonesia's Bintang Adipurna. Who was the first?
x: Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Indian PM to receive Bintang Adipurna, Indonesia's highest civilian honour.

s: Which of the following defence outcomes of PM Modi's July 2026 visit to Indonesia is NOT correct?
o: Indonesia became the second ASEAN nation to buy BrahMos
Indonesia placed the first international order for the Astra missile
Cooperation included technology transfer and industrial cooperation
Indonesia became the first ASEAN nation to buy BrahMos
x: Indonesia was the second ASEAN nation to buy BrahMos, not the first.

s: Which IIM's campus in Indonesia was an outcome of PM Modi's July 2026 visit?
x: The education outcome was an IIM Bangalore campus in Indonesia.

s: During the July 2026 visit to New Zealand, what major development took place in India–New Zealand relations?
o: A Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement was signed
The relationship was elevated to a Strategic Partnership
A Mutual Logistics Support Arrangement was terminated
New Zealand joined the Global Biofuels Alliance
x: The Prime Ministers of India and New Zealand met in Auckland on 11 July 2026, and the bilateral relationship was elevated to a Strategic Partnership. The Global Biofuels Alliance reference concerns New Zealand’s participation, not the headline outcome of the Auckland meeting.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India–New Zealand relations?
o: The Roadmap seeks to double trade to NZ$7 billion by 2030.
The Roadmap to 2030 established diplomatic relations for the first time.
x: Diplomatic relations date from 1952, so the Roadmap to 2030 did not establish them; it is non-binding and targets NZ$7 billion by 2030.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct in the context of the July 2026 India–New Zealand Strategic Partnership?
o: New Zealand's Prime Minister was Christopher Luxon
New Zealand's currency is the Australian Dollar
It was the first Indian PM's official visit to New Zealand in about 40 years
x: New Zealand's currency is the NZ Dollar.

s: In which year did India and Indonesia establish their Comprehensive Strategic Partnership?
x: The Comprehensive Strategic Partnership dates from 2018, not 2019.

s: Which of the following countries is a member of the G20?
x: Indonesia is a G20 member; Singapore, Malaysia and Vietnam are not.

s: With which dynasty is the 9th-century Prambanan Temple Complex in Indonesia associated?
x: Prambanan is a 9th-century Shaiva complex of the Sanjaya dynasty, a UNESCO site since 1991.

s: India and Indonesia will jointly develop which deep sea port near the Malacca Strait?
x: Sabang Deep Sea Port, near the Malacca Strait, is to be developed jointly by India and Indonesia.

s: Where is Bharat Dynamics Limited headquartered?
x: BDL is headquartered in Hyderabad; Gurugram hosts the IFC-IOR.

s: What does the cooperation between NCPOR and New Zealand's University of Canterbury relate to?
x: NCPOR–University of Canterbury cooperation is on Antarctic research; NIFTEM–Massey covers food technology.

s: Which country will host the 2030 Commonwealth Games, referred to in the India–New Zealand Joint Action Plan on Sport?
x: India, not New Zealand, hosts the 2030 Commonwealth Games.

s: The reference to Gallipoli in the India–New Zealand relationship is associated with which event?
o: The establishment of diplomatic relations in 1952
Indian soldiers serving with ANZAC in 1915
The launch of the Opening Doors to India initiative in 2011
The signing of the 2025 Defence Cooperation MoU
x: The Gallipoli reference concerns Indian soldiers serving with ANZAC in 1915. The other options relate to later diplomatic or institutional developments and not to the Gallipoli connection.

s: Under the India–New Zealand Strategic Partnership, with which body does India's NIA cooperate?
x: The police cooperation is between the NIA and New Zealand Police; the partnership also includes a 2025 Defence Cooperation MoU.

s: Which Indian missile got its first international order, from Indonesia, in July 2026?
x: Indonesia placed an export order for the Astra air-to-air missile, its first international order.

s: Where was the inaugural India–New Zealand Defence Strategic Dialogue held in 2025?
x: The inaugural Defence Strategic Dialogue was held in New Delhi in 2025.

s: With its July 2026 deal, Indonesia became which ASEAN nation to buy BrahMos?
x: Indonesia is the second ASEAN buyer of BrahMos, not the first.

s: Who among the following declared Indonesia's independence on 17 August 1945, along with Mohammad Hatta?
x: Indonesia's independence was declared on 17 August 1945 by Soekarno, Mohammad Hatta and Sutan Sjahrir.

s: BrahMos Aerospace, set up in 1998, is a joint venture of DRDO and which country's NPO Mashinostroyeniya?
x: BrahMos Aerospace is a DRDO-Russia (NPO Mashinostroyeniya) joint venture.

s: In India–Japan relations, which milestone–year pair is correctly matched?
x: Diplomatic relations began in 1952; the Global Partnership came in 2000, the Annual Summit in 2006 and CEPA in 2011.

s: In which year was the India–Japan Act East Forum set up and the Quad revived?
x: 2017 saw the Act East Forum and the Quad's revival; 2014 was the Special Strategic and Global Partnership.

s: In which field is the UNICORN stealth mast the first India–Japan co-manufacturing agreement?
x: UNICORN is a stealth naval mast and marks the first India–Japan co-manufacturing agreement in this area.

s: Who signed the India–Japan agreement to strengthen maritime security in August 2026?
x: The maritime-security agreement was signed by India’s Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and Japan’s Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi. Piyush Goyal is associated with the India–Japan Startup Roundtable, while Sanae Takaichi is Japan’s Prime Minister.

s: Which India–Japan exercise is associated with the two countries' navies?
x: JIMEX is the India–Japan naval exercise. Dharma Guardian is associated with the armies, Veer Guardian with the air forces, and Malabar involves India with the United States and Australia.

s: Where was the 16th India–Japan Annual Summit (1–3 July 2026), PM Sanae Takaichi's first official visit, held?
x: The summit was held in New Delhi; Visakhapatnam hosted the International Fleet Review 2026.

s: The India–Japan Cooperative Biogas for Growth Initiative supports India's target of how many biogas and organic fertiliser plants?
x: The target is 1,000 biogas and organic fertiliser plants.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the outcomes of the 16th India–Japan Annual Summit?
o: Toyama Prefecture is paired with Andhra Pradesh
LUPEX is the ISRO–JAXA lunar polar mission
Priority sections of the Mumbai–Ahmedabad HSR will begin commercial operation in 2030
Japan supports India's hosting of the 4th UN World Conference on Disaster Risk Reduction in 2030
x: Priority sections of the Mumbai–Ahmedabad HSR are to begin commercial operation in 2027, not 2030.

s: What is UNICORN, the first India–Japan defence co-development programme?
x: UNICORN (Unified Complex Radio Antenna) is a naval stealth mast, the first India–Japan co-development programme.

s: The India–Japan Joint Statement on AI from the 16th Annual Summit is linked to which initiative?
x: The summit launched the first India–Japan AI Strategic Dialogue and a Joint Statement on AI linked to the Hiroshima AI Process.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 16th India–Japan Annual Summit?
o: The summit date in the outcomes was 2 July 2026.
About 100 business cooperation agreements were signed.
Japan set a target of ¥10 trillion investment over the next decade.
It was held in New Delhi.
x: About 120, not 100, business agreements were signed; the other statements are correct.

s: Sanae Takaichi became the Prime Minister of which country?
x: Sanae Takaichi became Prime Minister of Japan and made her first visit to India in July 2026.

s: The 8th India-Japan Defence Policy Dialogue, which prepared the ground for the next 2+2 Ministerial Dialogue, was held at which place in July 2026?
x: The 8th India-Japan Defence Policy Dialogue was held in Tokyo in July 2026 and prepared the next 2+2 Ministerial Dialogue.

s: Which is the nodal body for Startup India, launched on 16 January 2016?
x: DPIIT, not NITI Aayog, is the nodal body for Startup India.

s: Dharma Guardian is the India–Japan exercise between which of their services?
x: Dharma Guardian is the Army exercise; JIMEX is naval and Veer Guardian is for the air forces.

s: Which countries take part in the Malabar naval exercise?
x: Malabar brings together the navies of India, Japan, the US and Australia.

s: India and Mauritius concluded a 5-year petroleum product supply contract in August 2026 with which company?
x: A G2G MoU on oil and gas and a 5-year petroleum supply contract with IOCL support Mauritius' energy security.

s: India and Singapore upgraded their relationship to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in which year?
x: India and Singapore established diplomatic ties in 1965, a Strategic Partnership in 2015, and a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in 2024. Therefore, 2024 is the correct answer; 2015 refers to the earlier Strategic Partnership.

s: The India–Mauritius energy agreements were signed during whose visit to Mauritius on 20–21 August 2026?
x: The agreements (a G2G MoU on oil and gas and a 5-year petroleum supply contract with IOCL) were signed during Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri's visit to Mauritius on 20–21 August 2026.

s: What Special Economic Package did India announce during PM Modi's Seychelles visit?
x: A $175 million Special Economic Package was announced, along with UPI by end-2026 and Seychelles joining CDRI.

s: PM Modi's 2026 Seychelles visit, hosted by President Patrick Herminie, produced how many outcomes?
x: The visit for Seychelles' 50th National Day produced 19 outcomes.

s: What was the parliamentary distinction associated with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s 2026 visit to Seychelles?
o: He was the first Indian Prime Minister to address an extraordinary sitting of the Seychelles National Assembly
He was the first Indian Prime Minister to address the French Parliament
He was the first Indian Prime Minister to address the African Union
He was the first Indian Prime Minister to address the Seychelles Senate
x: Narendra Modi became the first Indian Prime Minister to address an extraordinary sitting of the Seychelles National Assembly. The other institutions mentioned are not identified in this context.

s: Which honour was conferred on Prime Minister Narendra Modi during his Seychelles visit?
x: The honour conferred on Prime Minister Narendra Modi was “Guardian of the Blue Horizon.” The other titles are not the honour associated with the visit.

s: Seychelles, on the Mascarene Plateau, consists of about how many islands?
x: Seychelles has 155 islands on the Mascarene Plateau.

s: Under which initiative are India and Singapore cooperating on semiconductors?
x: Semiconductor cooperation between India and Singapore is being pursued under the Green Lane Initiative. The other options refer to a broader partnership, a ministerial forum, and a maritime heritage complex, respectively.

s: Where is the National Maritime Heritage Complex, at a Harappan dockyard site in Gujarat?
x: The National Maritime Heritage Complex is at Lothal, a Harappan dockyard site in Gujarat.

s: LAMITIYE is India's military exercise with which country?
x: LAMITIYE is the India–Seychelles exercise.

s: Where was the 4th India–Singapore Ministerial Roundtable (August 2026) held?
x: The 4th ISMR met in Singapore in August 2026, covering semiconductors, green hydrogen, digital payments and SMRs.

s: In which state is Lothal, a Harappan dockyard linked to India's ancient maritime history?
x: Lothal is a Harappan dockyard in Gujarat.

s: Which of the following countries is a producer of pepper?
x: Malaysia, India and Indonesia produce pepper; Singapore is only a spice trading and re-export hub.

s: What is the capital of Seychelles?
x: Victoria, on Mahé island, is the capital of Seychelles, Africa's smallest and least-populated country.

s: Who is the Prime Minister of Singapore?
x: Lawrence Wong is Singapore's PM; Tharman Shanmugaratnam is the President.

s: What assistance did India provide to the Maldives in June 2026?
o: Two BHISHM Cubes and an Army field hospital
35+ tonnes of earthquake relief through an IAF C-17
20,000 measles vaccine doses and about 3,000 tonnes of medical supplies
x: India provided the Maldives with 20,000 measles vaccine doses and approximately 3,000 tonnes of medical supplies. The earthquake relief, UNRWA contribution and BHISHM Cubes were associated with other assistance measures.

s: What is the 2030 bilateral trade target under the India–Uzbekistan Comprehensive Strategic Partnership?
x: The two sides signed 11 agreements and set a $5 billion trade target by 2030.

s: During the Prime Minister’s State visit to Uzbekistan on 29–30 August 2026, India and Uzbekistan elevated their relationship to which level?
x: India and Uzbekistan raised their ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership during the 29–30 August 2026 State visit. The visit also marked the 15th anniversary of their strategic partnership; the other options do not describe the announced upgrade.

s: Where did PM Modi hold talks with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev during his August 2026 visit?
x: The talks were held in Tashkent, not Samarkand.

s: The April 2026 edition of Exercise Dustlik (India–Uzbekistan) was held in which region?
x: The latest edition of Exercise Dustlik was held in Namangan Region in April 2026.

s: In which city is Uzbekistan's first IT Park, set up in 2019 on the Indian STPI model?
x: The first IT Park was set up in Tashkent in 2019 on the STPI model.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India and Uzbekistan?
o: Uzbekistan supports India's permanent seat on the UN Security Council
India holds the BRICS chair in 2026
Uzbekistan wants to join the International Solar Alliance but not the International Big Cat Alliance
Uzbekistan is a doubly landlocked country
x: The statement wrongly excludes the International Big Cat Alliance from Uzbekistan's interest.

s: Uzbekistan is one of only two doubly landlocked countries. Which is the other?
x: Uzbekistan and Liechtenstein are the only two doubly landlocked countries.

s: Who was the Prime Minister of Slovakia during the Indian PM's visit in June 2026?
x: Robert Fico was Slovakia's Prime Minister during the visit.

s: Who was sworn in as President of Hungary on 19 August 2026?
x: Former Supreme Court judge András Baka became President; Péter Magyar is Hungary's PM.

s: Which country–capital pair is correctly matched?
x: Bishkek is the capital of Kyrgyzstan; Kuala Lumpur is Malaysia's, Warsaw is Poland's and Jerusalem is Israel's.

s: Who became King of Norway after the death of King Harald V in 2026?
x: After Harald V died at 89, his son became King Haakon VIII.

s: What is the name of Norway's parliament?
x: Norway's parliament is the Storting.

s: What happened to the proposed 20% reimbursement fee on cargo transiting the Strait of Hormuz?

x: ICI – Italy Calls India concerns the legal migration of Indian nurses, not doctors. The other statements are correct: ties became a Special Strategic Partnership, and cooperation spans critical minerals, defence, AI and semiconductors, with support for IMEC.

s: The Leadership Group for Industry Transition (LeadIT) was launched in 2019 by India and which country?
x: LeadIT was launched by India and Sweden in 2019; Iceland joined LeadIT 2.0.

s: In which year was the US Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act (CAATSA) enacted?
x: CAATSA was enacted in 2017; it targets Russia, Iran and North Korea.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The International North–South Transport Corridor includes Southeast Asia
Chabahar is outside the Persian Gulf
The Shahid Beheshti terminal is run by India Ports Global Limited under a 10-year agreement of May 2024
CAATSA concerns Russia, Iran and North Korea
x: The 7,200-km INSTC covers India, Iran, Russia, Central Asia and Europe, not Southeast Asia.

s: What was the value of the 2018 S-400 Triumf deal between India and Russia?
x: The 2018 S-400 deal was worth $5.4 billion, and the US did not sanction India.

s: Which port is described as the rival project to India-backed Chabahar?
x: Pakistan's Gwadar is the rival to Chabahar, which lies on the Gulf of Oman.

s: Through which company does India run the Shahid Beheshti terminal at Chabahar under a 10-year agreement signed in May 2024?
x: India Ports Global Limited (IPGL) runs the Shahid Beheshti terminal under a 10-year agreement of May 2024.

s:
Consider the following statements about Chabahar:
1. It lies on the Gulf of Oman, outside the Persian Gulf.
2. It is Iran's only oceanic port.
3. The INSTC linked to it extends to Southeast Asia.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; the 7,200 km INSTC links India, Iran, Russia, Central Asia and Europe, not Southeast Asia.

s: The US law CAATSA (2017) mainly targets which countries?
x: CAATSA (Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act, 2017) targets Russia, Iran and North Korea.

s: What status did Canada get in the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) in March 2026?
x: Canada became a Dialogue Partner of IORA in March 2026.

s: India bought the S-400 Triumf air defence system in 2018 from which country?
x: The $5.4 billion S-400 deal was signed with Russia in 2018; the US did not impose CAATSA sanctions on India.

s: Which body was created as an outcome of the 1973 Oil Price Crisis?
x: The 1973 crisis was followed by the creation of the International Energy Agency.

s: India approached the IMF after which oil crisis?
x: India approached the IMF after the 1979 crisis, not after the 1973 crisis.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: 1973 oil embargo – Targeted countries opposing Israel
1973 oil embargo – Targeted countries supporting Israel
April 2026 oil disruption – Strait of Malacca
x: The 1973 embargo targeted countries supporting Israel; the Yom Kippur War was in 1973 and the 2026 disruption was at the Strait of Hormuz.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the 1973 and 1979 Oil Crises is incorrect?
o: The 1979 Oil Crisis was linked to OPEC price-stabilising cuts.
Territories lost in the 1967 war were among the other factors associated with the 1973 Oil Crisis.
The 1979 Oil Crisis was linked to the Iranian Revolution.
The end of the gold standard in 1971 was among the other factors associated with the 1973 Oil Crisis.
x: The incorrect statement is the first one: the 1979 Oil Crisis was linked to the Iranian Revolution, not to OPEC price-stabilising cuts. The end of the gold standard in 1971 and territories lost in the 1967 war were other factors behind the 1973 crisis.

s: Which of the following country–leader pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Mojtaba Khamenei is Iran's Supreme Leader; Iran's President is Masoud Pezeshkian.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India–Russia economic ties?
o: They set a trade target of USD 100 billion by 2030.
India–Russia trade stood at USD 128 billion in 2024–25.
They set a target of USD 50 billion in mutual investment by 2025.
After 2022, Russia became India's largest crude supplier.
x: India–Russia trade was USD 68.72 billion in 2024–25; USD 128 billion is roughly India–US trade.

s: What position did Russia attain among India's crude-oil suppliers after 2022?
x: After 2022, Russia became India's largest crude supplier.

s: In which year were India–Russia ties upgraded to a 'Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership'?
x: The upgrade came in 2010; 2000 saw the Declaration on Strategic Partnership.

s: Which development was reported regarding Kudankulam Units 1–6 during 2025?
o: All six units were permanently shut down after the delivery of Unit 6
The Unit 6 reactor vessel was delivered, alongside talks on SMRs and Units 7–8
Units 7–8 were commissioned and the Unit 6 reactor vessel was exported
Only Units 1–2 remained operational and talks on SMRs were abandoned
x: In 2025, the Unit 6 reactor vessel was delivered at Kudankulam, while talks continued on SMRs and Units 7–8. The other options reverse or alter these developments.

s: Where was WAVES 2025, attended by Russian Culture Minister Olga Lyubimova in May 2025, held?
x: Olga Lyubimova attended WAVES 2025 in Mumbai in May 2025.

s: At the 23rd India-Russia Annual Summit held in New Delhi in December 2025, India and Russia set which trade target for 2030?
x: India and Russia set a bilateral trade target of 100 billion dollars by 2030.

s: Which of the following is among the India–Russia connectivity initiatives?
x: The Chennai–Vladivostok maritime corridor is an India–Russia connectivity initiative, along with INSTC (India–Iran–Russia) and the proposed India–EAEU FTA. The other options are not India–Russia connectivity projects.

s: Which project is described as a flagship of India–Russia nuclear cooperation?
x: The Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant is the flagship of India–Russia nuclear cooperation. BrahMos concerns co-development, Sakhalin concerns energy investment, and INDRA is an exercise.

s: Through which Russian agency did India sign the 'Action Plan for Prioritization and Implementation of Cooperation Areas in the Nuclear Field'?
x: The nuclear-field Action Plan was signed with Russia through Rosatom.

s: BrahMos is named after the Brahmaputra and which Russian river?
x: BrahMos takes its name from the Brahmaputra and Moskva rivers.

s: Which of the following is a joint India–Russia development rather than a purchase or licence build?
x: BrahMos is jointly developed by DRDO and NPO Mashinostroyeniya; S-400 and INS Vikramaditya are purchases and Su-30MKI is licence-built by HAL.

s: Of the five S-400 Triumf regiments India purchased from Russia, how many had been delivered?
x: India bought 5 S-400 regiments, of which 3 have been delivered.

s: Which company makes the AK-203 rifles under India–Russia cooperation?
x: AK-203 is made by Indo-Russia Rifles Pvt Ltd; HAL licence-builds the Su-30MKI.

s: Annual India–Russia summits began with which development?
o: 1971 Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation
x: Annual summits began with the 2000 Declaration on Strategic Partnership; the 2010 upgrade was to a Special and Privileged one.

s: Which countries are linked by the International North–South Transport Corridor (INSTC)?
x: The INSTC is a multi-modal corridor connecting India, Iran and Russia.

s: In which year did India sign the Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation with the USSR?
x: The Indo-Soviet Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation was signed in 1971; annual summits began only after the 2000 Strategic Partnership.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 'Shadbhujii Coalition'?
o: It includes Greece and Cyprus along with India
IMEC was announced at the 2023 G20
It was announced by Israel's President Isaac Herzog
x: The coalition was announced by PM Benjamin Netanyahu, not President Isaac Herzog.

s: In which year did India recognise Israel?
x: India recognised Israel in 1950. The year 1992 refers to the establishment of full diplomatic ties, while the other years do not match the stated recognition milestone.

s: In which year did the India–UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) come into force?
x: The CEPA came into force in 2022; the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership dates to 2017.

s: During Operation Swadesh, about how many Indian medical students were estimated to be in Iran?
x: Around 10,000 Indians were in Iran, including 2,500–3,000 medical students.

s: Over what period did Israel target 50,000 more Indian workers after PM Modi's visit?
x: The target of 50,000 more Indian workers is for five years, not ten.

s: During Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan's visit to India, agreements covered which of the following sectors?
o: Agriculture, fisheries, tourism, textiles and banking
Nuclear energy, energy, railways, space and artificial intelligence
Defence, education, health, mining and aviation
Water, shipping, forests, sports and culture
x: The agreements covered nuclear energy, energy, railways, space and artificial intelligence. The other combinations do not represent the sectors identified for the visit.

s: Which country is a member of the I2U2 grouping along with India, Israel and the USA?
x: I2U2 = India, Israel, UAE and USA.

s: From which country did India evacuate its nationals under Operation Swadesh (January 2026)?
x: Operation Swadesh evacuated Indians from Iran amid anti-government protests.

s: Into which type of partnership were India–Israel ties expanded during PM Modi's historic visit to Israel?
x: PM Modi's visit expanded India–Israel ties into a Special Strategic Partnership, centred on peace, innovation and prosperity.

s: Which was the first Arab country to have a nuclear power plant?
x: The UAE's Barakah nuclear plant, working since 2020, made it the first Arab state with nuclear power.

s: In which year did India establish full diplomatic relations with Israel?
x: India recognised Israel in 1950 but set up full diplomatic ties only in 1992.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India recognised Israel in 1950.
2. India established full diplomatic ties with Israel in 1992.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: recognition came in 1950 and full diplomatic ties in 1992.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the India–US trade deal is incorrect?
o: The additional 25% punitive duty imposed over Russian oil purchases was removed.
India has regained Generalised System of Preferences (GSP), which was withdrawn in 2019.
India is expected to make purchases of up to USD 500 billion of US energy, agriculture, coal and technology.
Mission 500 aims to raise bilateral trade to USD 500 billion by 2030.
x: India has not regained GSP; it was withdrawn in 2019. The other statements correctly describe the removal of the additional 25% duty, expected purchases of up to USD 500 billion, and the Mission 500 target of USD 500 billion by 2030.

s: Amid US pressure on India's purchases of Russian oil, what did Donald Trump claim India had agreed to do under the India–US trade understanding?
o: Withdraw from the India–Russia strategic partnership
x: Donald Trump claimed that India had agreed to stop buying Russian oil under the India–US trade understanding. The claim concerned Russian oil purchases, not India's strategic partnership with Russia or its purchases from the United States.

s: Under the India–US trade deal, what will be the effective tariff burden on Indian goods, compared with the pre-deal level?
x: The effective burden is reduced from about 50% to 18%. The figure of 20% refers to the approximate tariff faced by Vietnam and Bangladesh, while 30–35% refers to China.

s: Which of the following groups was fully protected under the agricultural provisions of the India–US trade agreement?
o: Aircraft parts, generic drugs and diamonds
Dairy, poultry, meat and GM foods
x: Dairy, poultry, meat and GM foods were among the agricultural items fully protected. Spices, tea, coffee and cashew were among the exports facing zero additional duty, while the other options refer to industrial or non-agricultural sectors.

s: Which country saw a tariff on Indian goods reduced from 50 percent to 18 percent under the February 2026 trade deal?
x: Under the February 2026 India-US trade deal, the US tariff on India was reduced from 50 percent to 18 percent.

s: Which pre-deal Indian measure opened the nuclear sector to private players?
x: The SHANTI Act, 2025, opened India’s nuclear sector to private players. US–India COMPACT concerned military partnership, commerce and technology, while iCET concerned technology cooperation.

s: What is the full form of US–India COMPACT announced in 2025?
o: Coordinated Mechanism for Public Administration, Commerce & Technology
Comprehensive Organisation for Market Partnership, Agriculture, Commerce & Trade
Catalyzing Operations for Maritime Partnership, Accelerated Cooperation & Transport
Catalyzing Opportunities for Military Partnership, Accelerated Commerce & Technology
x: US–India COMPACT stands for Catalyzing Opportunities for Military Partnership, Accelerated Commerce & Technology. The other expansions do not correspond to the 2025 bilateral framework.

s: By which year does India–US 'Mission 500' aim at bilateral trade of USD 500 billion?
x: Mission 500 targets USD 500 billion of India–US trade by 2030.

s: What happened to India's GSP benefits, withdrawn in 2019, under the February 2026 India–US trade deal?
x: The deal did not restore GSP; the US tariff on India is now 18%, not zero.

s: Which rank does the United States hold among investors in India, with USD 70.65 billion during 2000–2025?
x: The US is the 3rd largest investor in India, with about USD 70.65 billion of investment from 2000 to 2025.

s: India’s Free Trade Agreement concluded in December 2025 marked its first FTA with which country?
x: The agreement concluded in December 2025 was India’s first FTA with New Zealand and was negotiated in a record nine months by a women-led team. Australia, China and Japan are listed as ASEAN FTA partners, but the agreement in question was with New Zealand.

s: Under the India–New Zealand FTA, India offered tariff relief on what share of New Zealand imports?
x: India offered tariff relief on 95% of New Zealand imports, 57% duty-free from day one; New Zealand gave zero duty on 100% of Indian exports.

s: Which of the following statements regarding products excluded by India from the India–New Zealand Free Trade Agreement is incorrect?
o: Dairy products such as milk, cheese, butter and yogurt were excluded.
x: Kiwifruit was not listed among the products excluded by India; it was identified under agricultural cooperation. Dairy products, onions and edible oils were among the exclusions.

s: Which of the following pairs of trade-agreement type and feature is correctly matched?
o: Partial Scope Agreement – Free movement of capital and labour
Free Trade Agreement – Common external tariff
x: A Customs Union adds a common external tariff. A Partial Scope Agreement covers limited goods, an FTA cuts tariffs among members while keeping own tariffs for others, and a Common Market adds free movement of capital and labour.

s: Under the India–New Zealand Free Trade Agreement, what FDI commitment did New Zealand make?
x: New Zealand committed to invest $20 billion over 15 years, with a clawback provision.

s: During the US military action in Venezuela in early January 2026, who were seized by US special forces in Caracas?
x: US special forces seized President Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores; Delcy Rodríguez then became interim president.

s: The UN Secretary-General called the US military action in Venezuela a 'dangerous precedent' because it had no mandate from which body?
x: The action lacked a UN Security Council mandate, which is why it was called a dangerous precedent.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the January 2026 US action in Venezuela?
o: Nicolás Maduro was first taken to the USS Iwo Jima
Maduro was detained in New York on narco-terrorism charges
Delcy Rodríguez was sworn in as Interim President after being named by Venezuelan courts
Venezuela described the action as a lawful extradition
x: Venezuela called the action a “kidnapping” and declared a state of external disturbance.

s: Which of the following doctrine pairs is correctly matched?
o: Truman Doctrine – Opposed European interference in the Americas
Roosevelt Corollary – Expansion of the Monroe Doctrine in 1904
'Don-roe Doctrine' – Articulated by James Monroe in 1823
x: The Roosevelt Corollary expanded the Monroe Doctrine in 1904. The Monroe Doctrine (1823) opposed European interference, the Truman Doctrine meant Cold War containment and 'Don-roe' refers to its revival.

s: In which year was the Monroe Doctrine, invoked by the United States over Venezuela, proclaimed?
x: The Monroe Doctrine was enunciated in 1823.

s: Under what circumstances did Delcy Rodríguez become interim President of Venezuela in January 2026?
o: Nicolás Maduro resigned after an election defeat
the United States seized Nicolás Maduro
the National Assembly impeached Nicolás Maduro
x: Delcy Rodríguez became interim President after the United States seized Nicolás Maduro.

s: What is the currency of Venezuela?
x: Venezuela's currency is the bolívar; the country is an OPEC member with the largest proven crude reserves.

s: The India–Nepal environment MoU focuses on conservation in which regions?
x: The MoU focuses on the Himalayan and Terai regions and covers forestry, wildlife, biodiversity and climate change.

s: Tarique Rahman was sworn in as Prime Minister of which country on 17 February 2026?
x: Tarique Rahman of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party was sworn in as Prime Minister of Bangladesh on 17 February 2026 after the parliamentary election.

s: Who was Nepal's Prime Minister when the India–Nepal Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty on criminal matters was signed?
x:
Sushila Karki was interim PM until March 2026 – now Balendra (Balen) Shah (RSP), sworn in 27 March 2026 (app notes 6:69 sub 8)
The MLAT was signed while Sushila Karki (former Chief Justice) was Nepal's interim Prime Minister (from September 2025, after the Gen Z protests); Ram Chandra Poudel is the President. (Now Balendra (Balen) Shah, PM since 27 March 2026.)

s: What was the value of the aid package for Seychelles announced by PM Modi after talks with President Dr Patrick Herminie?
x: India announced a $175 million aid package for Seychelles.

s: With which Indian vision was the $175 million aid package to Seychelles linked?
x: The Seychelles package was linked to Vision MAHASAGAR, which extends SAGAR (2015).

s: India's USD 450 million package for Sri Lanka after Cyclone Ditwah included how much as concessional credit?
x: The package had USD 350 million in concessional credit and USD 100 million in grants.

s: What was the name of India's relief operation that delivered more than 1,100 tonnes of relief on the day of Cyclone Ditwah?
x: Operation Sagar Bandhu delivered more than 1,100 tonnes of relief on the day of Cyclone Ditwah. The other operation names are not associated with this relief effort in the stated information.

s: The Ganga Water Sharing Treaty, signed in 1996, is scheduled to expire in which month and year?
x: The Ganga Water Sharing Treaty was signed on 12 December 1996 for 30 years and is scheduled to expire in December 2026. December 1996 was the month and year of signing, not its expiry.

s: What is the full form of SAGAR (2015), India's maritime vision for the Indian Ocean Region?
o: Safety and Growth Across the Region
Security and Governance for All in the Region
Sustainable Growth for All in the Region
Security and Growth for All in the Region
x: SAGAR stands for Security and Growth for All in the Region and casts India as a net security provider in the IOR.

s: What is the installed capacity of the Wangchhu Hydroelectric Project in Bhutan, on which the Adani Group began work?
x: Wangchhu has an installed capacity of 570 MW (4 × 142.5 MW).

s: On which date did India and Pakistan first exchange lists of nuclear installations?
x: The agreement was signed on 31 December 1988; the first exchange took place on 1 January 1992.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Ganga Water Sharing Treaty:
1. It governs dry-season flows at Farakka in West Bengal.
2. Earlier temporary arrangements were made in 1977, 1982 and 1986.
3. It can be renewed without mutual consent.
Which of the above is/are correct?
x: Only 1 is correct. The earlier arrangements were in 1977, 1982 and 1985, and renewal requires mutual consent.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Wangchhu Hydroelectric Project in Bhutan?
o: The Wangchu is called Raidak in India
It supplies winter power to India
The Wangchu is a tributary of the Brahmaputra
x: It is reversed: winter power goes to Bhutan and the summer surplus to India.

s: In which year was MAHASAGAR, which extends SAGAR to the Global South and the Indo-Pacific, announced?
x: SAGAR dates to 2015; MAHASAGAR (2025) extends it to the Global South and Indo-Pacific.

s:
Consider the following statements about SAGAR:
1. It was announced in 2015.
2. It projects India as a net security provider in the Indian Ocean Region.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: SAGAR (Security and Growth for All in the Region, 2015) casts India as net security provider in the IOR.

s: What share does Druk Green Power hold in the joint venture for Bhutan's Wangchhu project?
x: The JV is Druk Green Power 51% and Adani Power 49%.

s: Who founded the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) in 1978?
x: The BNP, which won the February 2026 election, was founded in 1978 by Ziaur Rahman.

s: What is the approximate length of the India–Bangladesh border?
x: India shares about 4,096 km of border with Bangladesh, its longest land border.

s: For how many years was the Ganga Water Sharing Treaty signed on 12 December 1996?
x: The treaty was signed for 30 years, so it expires in December 2026.

s: Which of the following countries was among the 23 countries with which India signed MoUs on Digital Public Infrastructure and India Stack?
x: Mongolia was among the countries included in India’s Digital Public Infrastructure and India Stack MoUs. The United Arab Emirates, Bhutan and France were associated with UPI availability, not the specified MoU list.

s: What new dialogue framework was established in the India–Canada reset?
o: A new G7-level trade dialogue framework
A new NSA-level security dialogue framework
x: The India–Canada reset included a new NSA-level security dialogue framework. The other three options are not the framework identified in the bilateral reset.

s: In which year was NATO, headquartered in Brussels, established, and who is its Secretary-General from 1 October 2024?
x: NATO was established in 1949, is headquartered in Brussels, and Mark Rutte is Secretary-General from 1 October 2024.

s: By which year have India and Canada set a CEPA target of USD 70 billion?
x: The India–Canada CEPA target is USD 70 billion by 2030.

s: When did Mark Carney become Prime Minister of Canada?
x: Carney became PM in March 2025 after Justin Trudeau stepped down in January 2025.

s: Which of the following is a Partner, not a Guest, in the US-led PAX SILICA initiative?
x: The UK and Japan are Partners; Taiwan, Canada and the EU are Guests.

s: Where did the European Union set up its first 'Legal Gateway' office outside its member countries?
x: The EU's first Legal Gateway office outside its member states is in New Delhi, guiding Indians on legal migration to the 27 EU states.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's Digital Public Infrastructure outreach?
o: India signed DPI or India Stack MoUs with 23 countries
DigiLocker pacts covered Cuba, Kenya, the UAE and Lao PDR
The India Stack Global Portal offered 18 platforms
x: UPI was available in eight countries, not 23; 23 is the number of countries with DPI or India Stack MoUs.

s: Who launched Arctic Sentry for security in the Arctic and the High North?
x: NATO launched Arctic Sentry; it is not a military operation with permanent troops.

s: With reference to NATO's Arctic Sentry, which pair is correctly matched?
x: Denmark's Arctic Endurance is associated with Greenland. Cold Response is Norway's, Joint Force Command Norfolk is in the USA, and Arctic Sentry coordinates with both exercises.

s: Which group of countries condemned the United States military action in Venezuela in January 2026?
o: Japan, Australia, New Zealand and South Korea
x: Russia, China, Iran and Cuba condemned the US military action in Venezuela, while the EU urged restraint. The other options list countries not identified as the condemning group.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Weimar Triangle?
o: It consists of France, Germany and Poland
It was established on 29 August 1991 at Weimar
It has a formal institutional structure
S. Jaishankar's meeting with it was India's first-ever engagement
x: The Weimar Triangle has no formal institutional structure.

s: By how many years was the India–Fiji Agriculture MoU extended at the talks of 9 January 2026?
x: The MoU was extended by five years and a Joint Working Group was to be set up.

s: Who leads PAX SILICA, the initiative to secure supply chains in silicon, semiconductors, AI and critical minerals?
x: PAX SILICA is a US-led initiative covering these sectors.

s: Which of the following is NOT a member of the G7?
x: The G7 is Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, UK and US; Russia was in the G8 from 1998.

s: Hardeep Nijjar, whose killing triggered the 2023 India–Canada crisis, was killed in which Canadian province?
x: The Nijjar killing (June 2023) took place in British Columbia, not Ontario.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 2023 India–Canada diplomatic crisis?
o: Justin Trudeau alleged an Indian role in the killing of Hardeep Nijjar.
Diplomats were expelled and High Commissioners withdrawn.
The alleged killing took place in Ontario.
The crisis followed an allegation by Canada's Prime Minister.
x: The case was linked to British Columbia, not Ontario; the other statements are correct.

s: Students from which country form the largest international student group in Canada?
x: Indian students (3.92 lakh in December 2024) are the largest international student group in Canada.

s: In which year did the G7 become the G8 with the inclusion of Russia?
x: Russia joined in 1998, making the G7 the G8.

s: Where was the World Economic Forum, whose President Børge Brende resigned over Epstein links, established in 1971?
x: The WEF was established in 1971 at Cologny in Geneva.

s: Who became the youngest Prime Minister in Dutch history in February 2026?
x: Rob Jetten, a member of D66, became the youngest Prime Minister in Dutch history at the age of 38. Andrey Gurov became Bulgaria's interim Prime Minister, while Anutin Charnvirakul and Tariq Rahman are associated with Thailand and Bangladesh respectively.

s: By whom was José María Balkazar of Peru Libre elected as Peru's president?
x: Balkazar was elected by Peru's 130-member Congress.

s: Who was Japan's Prime Minister when Japan issued an alert after North Korean missile launches in January 2026?
x: Sanae Takaichi was the Prime Minister of Japan at the time.

s: In the February 2026 Japanese election, the LDP won how many of the 465 seats?
x: The LDP won 271 of 465 seats (majority mark 261); Thailand's Bhumjaithai won 194 of 500.

s: Andrey Gurov was appointed interim Prime Minister of which country?
x: Andrey Gurov, Deputy Governor of the Bulgarian National Bank, was appointed Bulgaria's interim PM by President Iliana Lotova.

s: Mia Amor Mottley, who won a third term in February 2026 by winning all 30 seats, is the Prime Minister of which country?
x: Mia Amor Mottley of the Barbados Labour Party won all 30 seats and a third term in Barbados.

s: Which former President of South Korea was sentenced to life imprisonment over the martial law of 3 December 2024?
x: Ex-President Yoon Suk Yeol got life imprisonment for declaring martial law on 3 December 2024.

s: Which party, led by caretaker PM Anutin Charnvirakul, emerged as the largest party in Thailand's February 2026 election?
x: Bhumjaithai won 194 of 500 seats, ahead of the People's Party (116) and Pheu Thai (76).

s: What is RELOS, signed between India and Russia in February 2025 and operationalised in June 2026?
x: RELOS is the India–Russia logistics pact, signed in February 2025 and operationalised in June 2026.

s: Where was the 13th edition of the multilateral naval exercise MILAN (February 2026) hosted?
x: MILAN 2026 was held at Visakhapatnam on 15–25 February 2026 along with the International Fleet Review.

s: Exercise Dharma Guardian 2026, held at Chaubattia in Uttarakhand, is an Army exercise between India and which country?
x: Dharma Guardian is the India–Japan Army exercise; INDRA is the India–Russia series.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Zapad-2025 was hosted by Russia; India only took part in it.

s: Which period does the India–Russia military-technical cooperation agreement cover?
x: The India–Russia military-technical cooperation agreement covers 2021–2031.

s: By which year have India and the UAE set a target of USD 200 billion in bilateral trade?
x: The India–UAE bilateral trade target is USD 200 billion by 2032.

s: Venezuela possesses approximately how many barrels of proven crude oil reserves?
x: Venezuela has approximately 300 billion barrels of proven crude reserves.
